deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 12% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.0% = 10-year Treasury 5.0% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (6%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 21% last year; 37%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity 1% (3 years ago -937%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $22.5B, up 0% from a year ago — about 8.5× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $1.7B, up 88% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 112% vs quarterly sales up 22% (days to collect 21 → 36). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.
Inventory up 59% vs quarterly sales up 22% (days of inventory 26 → 36). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 37%/yr over 3 years; operating margin today -0% vs a 4-year range of -24–-0% (median -7%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Operating margin -0%: it spends more to run the business than it earns from sales.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.read: You pay 575× last year's profit; only 49× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.
